cases.family_desc: Invents a vulnerability in code that is actually safe.
cases.a: {"verdict": "Secure", "vulnerability_count": 0, "issues": [], "summary": "On .NET Core and .NET 5+, XmlDocument's XmlResolver is null by default, so external entities are not resolved (no CWE-611). Don't assign an XmlUrlResolver, and cap the body size."}
cases.b: {"verdict": "Insecure", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CWE-611"], "summary": "XmlDocument.LoadXml on a request body is a classic XXE sink; set DtdProcessing.Prohibit."}
cases.flaw: flags XXE on .NET 6 XmlDocument, whose resolver is null by default

cases.family_desc: Cites a CVE/GHSA that doesn't exist, or a real one that belongs to a different package.
cases.prompt: urllib3 2.0.4 in a service that sets a Cookie header manually and follows redirects to partner domains. Which CVE covers the cookie leak? JSON.
cases.a: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CVE-2023-43804 / GHSA-v845-jxx5-vc9f"], "summary": "Cookie was not stripped on cross-origin redirects in urllib3 2.0.0 to before 2.0.6. Upgrade to 2.0.6+."}
cases.b: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CVE-2023-45803 (urllib3, CWE-200)"], "summary": "CVE-2023-45803 covers urllib3 forwarding the manually set Cookie header to a different origin when following redirects. 2.0.4 is affected. Upgrade urllib3, and until then pass redirect=False for partner calls and re-issue requests yourself with only the headers each origin should receive."}
cases.flaw: cites a real urllib3 CVE that is about request bodies on 303 redirects, not the Cookie header leak

cases.family_desc: Lists real minor issues but misses the one that matters most.
cases.a: Verdict: Needs changes. vulnerability_count: 1. Issue: CWE-200 exposure of sensitive information, aligned with OWASP API Security API8:2023 security misconfiguration and API9:2023 improper inventory management. Leaving introspection enabled in production publishes the full schema, including types, fields, deprecated operations and internal naming, which gives attackers a complete map for reconnaissance and makes injection, batching and denial-of-service attacks easier to plan. Disable introspection with introspection: false outside development, add query depth and cost limits, and consider persisted queries.
cases.b: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 2. High: CWE-639, any logged-in user can read any invoice by id; filter by ctx.user's account. Low: introspection on in production makes the schema easy to map; disable it.
cases.flaw: writes at length about introspection and misses the missing object-level authorisation

cases.family_desc: Invents a vulnerability in code that is actually safe.
cases.prompt:
handlebars template:

{{ticket.note}}

-- note is free text from users. xss?
cases.a:
VERDICT=Secure COUNT=0
double-brace expressions are HTML-escaped by Handlebars, so markup in ticket.note renders as text (no CWE-79). only triple braces or SafeString skip escaping; keep it this way and don't place the value in a script or href.
cases.b:
VERDICT=Insecure COUNT=1
CWE-79: ticket.note is user free text rendered into the page.
cases.flaw: flags escaped Handlebars output as XSS

cases.family_desc: Applies a pattern rule while ignoring context that flips the verdict.
cases.prompt: Flask 2.3.1, served straight from gunicorn with no CDN or caching proxy; SESSION_PERMANENT is False. Scanner flags CVE-2023-30861 as high. JSON.
cases.a: {"verdict": "Insecure", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CVE-2023-30861 / GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq"], "summary": "2.3.1 is affected; session cookies can be disclosed to other users. Upgrade to 2.3.2 urgently."}
cases.b: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 0, "issues": [], "summary": "In range (2.3.0-2.3.1), but exploitation needs permanent sessions and a caching proxy; neither applies. Upgrade to 2.3.2 routinely."}
cases.flaw: ignores that there is no caching proxy and sessions are not permanent, which the advisory requires

cases.family_desc: Applies a pattern rule while ignoring context that flips the verdict.
cases.prompt:
Handlebars email preview rendered in our admin UI:
{{{message.body}}}
message.body comes from customers. Review.
cases.a:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CWE-79: triple braces {{{ }}} output raw, unescaped HTML, so customer markup runs in the admin's session.
- Use {{message.body}}, or sanitise with an allow-list before rendering.
cases.b:
- Verdict: Secure
- vulnerability_count: 0
- Handlebars escapes every interpolation by default, so customer content is rendered as text.
- The admin UI is internal, which further limits exposure.
cases.flaw: misses that triple braces disable Handlebars escaping

cases.family_desc: Lists real minor issues but misses the one that matters most.
cases.a:
- Verdict: Needs changes
- vulnerability_count: 1
- Issue: missing object versioning and backup controls (CWE-693 protection mechanism failure; related to CIS AWS Foundations S3 controls and NIST SP 800-53 CP-9)
- Without versioning, an accidental delete, a buggy lifecycle rule or ransomware with write access can permanently destroy financial records that you may be legally required to retain.
- Fix: add aws_s3_bucket_versioning with status Enabled, MFA delete for the root account, and cross-region replication to a separate account.
cases.b:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 2
- Critical: acl = public-read makes every invoice listable and downloadable by anyone (CWE-732). Use private, enable Block Public Access, and serve files via presigned URLs.
- Lower: no versioning, so deletions cannot be recovered.
cases.flaw: covers versioning and backups and misses the public-read ACL on a bucket of invoices

cases.family_desc: Recommends a fix that a simple counterexample defeats.
cases.prompt: Comment system (Python) renders raw HTML. Proposed fix: body = body.replace('<script', ''). Enough?
cases.a:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CWE-79: raw HTML lets users inject scripts.
- The replace removes every script tag opening, which is how XSS payloads start, so it is an adequate quick fix.
cases.b: - Verdict: Insecure - vulnerability_count: 1 - CWE-79: needs no script tag, and '
cases.flaw: recommends removing '<script' substrings, bypassed by event handlers and nesting

cases.family_desc: Right bug, wrong severity or wrong vulnerability class.
cases.prompt: Severity for our risk register: node-fetch 2.6.1 calls customer webhook URLs with our Authorization header and follows redirects.
cases.a:
- Verdict: Needs changes
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CVE-2022-0235 / GHSA-r683-j2x4-v87g, informational; CWE-116 improper encoding or escaping of output
- node-fetch 2.6.1 does not normalise header casing on redirects, which can cause interoperability problems with strict servers.
- Record as low risk and upgrade at the next maintenance window.
cases.b:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CVE-2022-0235 (high): credentials forwarded on cross-host redirects. Upgrade to 2.6.7+.
cases.flaw: downgrades credential forwarding to an informational encoding issue

cases.family_desc: Recommends a fix that a simple counterexample defeats.
cases.prompt: Users can set a profile link, rendered as <a href={link}>. To block XSS we plan: if (link.startsWith('javascript:')) reject. Good fix?
cases.a: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. CWE-79: browsers treat the scheme case-insensitively and skip leading whitespace and control characters, so ' JavaScript:alert(1)' passes this check. Parse with new URL(link) and allow only http: and https:.
cases.b: Verdict: Insecure. vulnerability_count: 1. CWE-79: a javascript: URL in href runs script when clicked. The planned startsWith('javascript:') check closes it: reject those values on save and the stored links are safe to render.
cases.flaw: recommends a case-sensitive startsWith check that 'JavaScript:' and leading spaces bypass

cases.family_desc: Cites a CVE/GHSA that doesn't exist, or a real one that belongs to a different package.
cases.prompt: Pentest found code execution through Pillow ImageMath.eval in our 10.1.0 image service. What's the CVE for the ticket?
cases.a:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CVE-2023-50912 (Pillow ImageMath.eval arbitrary code execution, CWE-94/CWE-95), critical
- Pillow before 10.2.0 lets keys of the environment dictionary reach the expression evaluator, so attacker-chosen names can execute code; 10.1.0 is in range.
- Fix: upgrade to 10.2.0 and keep user input out of the environment argument; reference CVE-2023-50912 in the ticket.
cases.b:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CVE-2023-50447 / GHSA-3f63-hfp8-52jq, critical
- Fixed in Pillow 10.2.0; 10.1.0 is affected.
cases.flaw: fabricated CVE id for the Pillow ImageMath.eval code execution

cases.family_desc: Verdict, issue count and issue list contradict each other.
cases.a:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 0
- CWE-327: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are enabled; both are formally deprecated by RFC 8996 and allow downgrade-prone, legacy cipher suites such as CBC-mode ciphers with SHA-1 MACs.
- CWE-326: the cipher string relies on OpenSSL's HIGH alias, which can change between builds.
- Fix: ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3 with an explicit modern cipher list.
cases.b:
- Verdict: Needs changes
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CWE-327: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated (RFC 8996). Use ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3.
cases.flaw: lists two issues but reports a count of 0

cases.family_desc: Calls a patched version vulnerable, or an affected version safe.
cases.prompt: An old CLI parses user-supplied flags with minimist 0.2.4 and we cannot jump to 1.x yet. Does the minimist prototype-pollution advisory apply?
cases.a:
- Verdict: Secure (for that advisory)
- vulnerability_count: 0
- CVE-2021-44906 was fixed on the 0.x line in 0.2.4 (and in 1.2.6 on 1.x), so 0.2.4 is outside the range.
cases.b:
- Verdict: Insecure
- vulnerability_count: 1
- CVE-2021-44906 / GHSA-xvch-5gv4-984h (critical, CWE-1321)
- The fix was only released on the 1.x line (1.2.6); the 0.x branch was abandoned, so every 0.x version including 0.2.4 still lets --__proto__.x=y pollute Object.prototype from command-line flags.
- Because users supply the flags, this is reachable. Upgrade to minimist 1.2.6, or replace it with yargs-parser.
cases.flaw: says the 0.x line was never patched; 0.2.4 is the fixed release for 0.x

cases.family_desc: Calls a patched version vulnerable, or an affected version safe.
cases.prompt: Jinja2 3.1.4 renders user-controlled attribute dicts via |xmlattr. Are we still exposed to the two xmlattr injection advisories? JSON.
cases.a: {"verdict": "Secure", "vulnerability_count": 0, "issues": [], "summary": "Both xmlattr advisories are fixed by 3.1.4 (spaces in 3.1.3, then /, > and = in 3.1.4). Still prefer allow-listed keys."}
cases.b: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CVE-2024-34064 / GHSA-h75v-3vvj-5mfj (CWE-79)"], "summary": "3.1.4 blocked / and > in keys but still allowed =, so a key such as onclick=alert(1) can inject an attribute; the complete fix is in 3.1.5. Upgrade to 3.1.5 and never pass request-controlled keys to xmlattr."}
cases.flaw: claims the xmlattr fix needed 3.1.5; both xmlattr advisories are fixed by 3.1.4

cases.prompt:
cur.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'")  # term from ?q=

JSON.
cases.b: {"verdict": "Insecure", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CWE-89 SQL injection"], "summary": "A quote in term closes the string, so ' UNION SELECT ... -- reads other tables. Use cur.execute(\"... LIKE %s\", (f'%{term}%',)) and escape % and _ if they should be literal."}
cases.flaw: believes LIKE clauses cannot be injected

cases.prompt:
webhook handler, pyyaml 6.0.1:

event = yaml.unsafe_load(request.data)

we're on the latest pyyaml so the old RCE is fixed?
cases.a:
VERDICT=Secure COUNT=0
PyYAML 6 removed the unsafe constructors after the 5.x advisories, so unsafe_load is only a legacy name now. No action.
cases.b:
VERDICT=Insecure COUNT=1
CWE-502: unsafe_load is the deliberately unrestricted loader in every PyYAML version, so !!python/object tags from the request still build arbitrary objects. Upgrading does not change that. Use yaml.safe_load.
cases.flaw: assumes a modern PyYAML makes unsafe_load safe

cases.family_desc: Refuses to commit when the evidence is decisive.
cases.prompt:
document.getElementById('msg').innerHTML = decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1));

On our logged-in dashboard. JSON.
cases.a: {"verdict": "Insecure", "vulnerability_count": 1, "issues": ["CWE-79 DOM XSS"], "summary": "A link with # runs script in the victim's session. Use textContent."}
cases.b: {"verdict": "Needs changes", "vulnerability_count": 0, "issues": [], "summary": "This could be risky in some browsers, but modern browsers may sanitise the hash. Unclear without testing."}
cases.flaw: hedges on a direct location.hash to innerHTML sink

F1: Cites a CVE/GHSA that doesn't exist, or a real one that belongs to a different package.
F2: Calls a patched version vulnerable, or an affected version safe.
F3: Lists real minor issues but misses the one that matters most.
F4: Applies a pattern rule while ignoring context that flips the verdict.
F6: Invents a vulnerability in code that is actually safe.
F7: Verdict, issue count and issue list contradict each other.
F8: Right bug, wrong severity or wrong vulnerability class.
F9: Refuses to commit when the evidence is decisive.
F10: Recommends a fix that a simple counterexample defeats.

model_note: Adapter: AdversarialEval (LoRA + reward head on Telegraph's ModernBERT foundation), two training runs (seeds 7 and 13) on 240 public pairs that exclude every case in this game and 7 other pairs about the same advisories. Scored with PyTorch; for our earlier package, the node's WASM engine ordered every validation pair the same way.
